ledger.claim: POL-NS-01 limb (d) is not satisfied on this record. The trip was terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, and the clause names that code as the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider: it is expressly excluded from the three codes limb (d) recognises (RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE, EXCESSIVE_WAIT). With limb (d) broken, the baseline chargeable no-show fails, and the $4.00 cancellation fee cannot stand.

There is not one qualifying in-radius fix anywhere in the trace. The driver's own GPS track carries 52 fixes between 15:03:30 and 15:18:40 and 0 of them fall inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius; his closest approach to the pickup pin over the entire trace is 284.95 m. POL-NS-02 therefore places the driver outside the arrival geofence for the whole 15 minutes preceding the cancellation, and POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails with it — on this record the driver never arrived at the pickup point. No accuracy-filter dispute is even available: there are no in-radius fixes to argue about.

Independently of arrival, the waiting-period arithmetic fails and POL-NS-06 decides the fee. The effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds (longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec 0.0, run_count 0) against a LARGE_VENUE minimum of 300 seconds — a shortfall of the full 300 seconds on the trace's own shortfall_basis. Limb (i) cannot rescue the fee: accumulation requires separate in-geofence intervals, and the trace shows zero of them (run_count 0, accumulated_sec 0.0), so there is no second interval to add to a first. The $4.00 cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full.

Even on the driver's own account this is a wrong-entrance case, not a rider no-show. His closest approach to the pickup pin over the whole trace is 284.95 m — outside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius, but comfortably inside the 400 m ceiling POL-NS-03 uses — and trip_record records a wait_time_min of 6.6, consistent with the driver's account of holding position rather than abandoning the pickup. The pickup pin carries venue_id VEN-VIVOCITY and the driver's track carries no venue_id at all, so the venue-match question is simply not established either way and, exactly as POL-NS-03 directs, the 400 m distance test governs alone. On that test the driver did not arrive at the pickup point, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the fee is refunded to the rider in full. Whichever of POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-03 governs these facts, the rider's remedy is the same full refund.

The rider was told 'Your driver has arrived' at 15:12:06 and read it at 15:12:22, while his own device sat within 22.5 m of the pin. The platform itself told him the driver was at the pickup point at a moment when the driver's trace shows he had never been inside the arrival radius at any time in the trip. That mislocation cannot be laid at the rider's door, and under POL-NS-03 the fault allocation must run against pin ambiguity rather than against him; POL-NS-02 confirms the same, because a rider who is at the pin cannot be the reason the pickup failed.

Under POL-NS-03 the fault is allocated to pin ambiguity on this record: the chat log holds only two SYSTEM messages and neither party specified a sub-location, while trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 4 — two or more — so limb (ii) applies rather than limb (i). That limb produces a platform-funded goodwill payment to the driver of 50 percent of the cancellation fee, SGD 2.00 of SGD 4.00, which POL-NS-03 says is charged to the platform and never recovered from the rider. Per POL-GEN-03 the rider's refund and the driver's goodwill are independent and are never netted, so the rider still recovers the whole $4.00.

The rider was where the pin was. The rider track carries 31 fixes between 15:08:20 and 15:21:00, every one of them qualifying, and the farthest any fix sits from the pickup pin is 22.5 m — far inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider-presence radius. There is therefore no rider-side failure that explains the null pickup, and no adverse inference about rider location can be drawn against him. I state plainly that POL-NS-04's own exoneration route is not open on this record — the chat log contains no rider message, so limb (a) cannot be run — and the refund does not depend on that clause.

No traffic advisory covers this pickup road. EV-ADVIS-00206-01 is MISSING — it has no payload and carries weight 0.0 — so there is no KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT that could have made holding position at the pin lawfully impossible, and POL-NS-06 limb (i) has nothing to work with. I am citing the absence itself, as an absence is citable, not asserting limb (i) in anyone's favour: the point is that a 300-second shortfall cannot be excused by an advisory that does not exist, and I disclose the artifact's weight of 0.0 as POL-GEN-02 requires.

No part of this fee may be paid out to the driver from the rider's money. POL-NS-07 compensates the driver only 'where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full', and it is not: limbs (b) and (d) both fail on this record. The anti-farming check is never reached, and on the citable fields it would pass in any event — driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d of 1 against driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 187. POL-NS-07 in any case never licenses a monetary ruling in the rider's favour, so it cannot be used to offset or reduce the refund.

Nothing here justifies holding the fee open instead of refunding it, so POL-NS-09 should not be triggered. Its limbs are all absent: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, and rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, so limbs (c) and (d) cannot fire, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming branch does not trip on 1 termination against 187 completed trips. The evidence on the deciding facts is also clean — the trace runs the full window at 100 percent coverage with 52 driver fixes and no gap over 120 seconds, the chat log's 2 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count, and the arrival marker falls inside the trace rather than 90 seconds away from it — so no limb of POL-NS-08 is engaged, POL-NS-09(e) is not reached, and the PARTIAL_REFUND cap does not apply. This case should be refunded now, not escalated.

The sum in dispute is the whole of the charge and it reconciles exactly. fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee is SGD 4.00, which equals both the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee under fee_schedule.resolution_rule, so the charged line is the correct amount and there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect to discount it by. The refund is therefore the full SGD 4.00, which is what POL-GEN-03's FULL_REFUND means here: the filing party, the rider, is entirely right and the whole contested amount returns.

On the platform's own derived numbers the driver never entered the pickup geofence: across a 52-fix trace his closest reported position is 284.95 m from the pin, and the arrival block records 0 qualifying in-radius fixes out of 52 driver fixes. POL-NS-01 limb (b) therefore fails and the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01 — this is not a no-show case at all, and POL-NS-02 itself routes a stationary-within-400 m hold to POL-NS-03.

Limb (d) of POL-NS-01 fails independently of the GPS: the trip was terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which is none of the three codes limb (d) recognises (RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE, EXCESSIVE_WAIT), and POL-NS-01 expressly directs that such a trip 'is decided under POL-NS-03'. The category's anchor clause cannot carry the charge.

The driver's closest approach of 284.95 m sits outside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius but comfortably inside POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling. That 400 m ceiling is, in the clause's own words, 'the whole test and is decidable from coordinates alone' — the measure places the driver where a driver who reached the pickup area and held at the wrong face of it would be, not a driver who never came to the venue. No venue_id match is asserted here; the distance test governs alone.

The driver held that position well beyond the required dwell: the trip record puts arrival at 15:12:05 and cancellation at 15:18:40, a 395 second wait recorded as 6.6 minutes, against the 300 second LARGE_VENUE minimum in fee_schedule.minimum_dwell_sec, and the driver's trace includes a stationary 0.0 km/h reading. The stationary-dwell condition of POL-NS-03 is met on the platform's own telemetry.

Fault under POL-NS-03 limb (i) cannot be laid on the driver. The chat log holds exactly two messages and both were sent by SYSTEM ('Driver assigned. Meet at VivoCity, Lobby L.' and 'Your driver has arrived'). The rider never stated an entrance, block, tower or bay in the chat, so the limb (i) trigger — a rider-stated sub-location the driver failed to move to — is simply absent.

Limb (ii) therefore governs the fault allocation: neither party specified a sub-location, and trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 4 — 2 or more — so the mislocation is attributed to pin ambiguity rather than to either party, and the driver is entitled to a platform-funded goodwill payment of 50 percent of the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee, that is SGD 2.00, charged to the platform and never recovered from the rider.

The false-arrival clause does not bite on this record. The only distance fact on the record is the trace's closest approach of 284.95 m, inside the 300 m mark POL-NS-05 uses, and POL-NS-05 expressly carves out 'a driver who is stationary within 300 m of the pin but outside the arrival radius when marking arrival', who is 'decided under POL-NS-03'. No admissible fact places the driver beyond 300 m at the 15:12:05 marker, so the shortfall limb of POL-NS-05 (which would withdraw all driver compensation) is not engaged.

The rider's exonerating clause is not engaged either. POL-NS-04 limb (a) requires a message sent by the rider during the waiting window whose content is locating or coordinating; the chat log contains no rider message at all, both entries being SYSTEM notifications. With limb (a) failed, the clause that would refund the fee 'with no driver compensation payable' does not apply.

POL-NS-06's shortfall arithmetic cannot strip the driver's compensation on these facts. POL-NS-02 says in terms that where the driver was stationary for the required dwell within 400 m of the pin, 'POL-NS-03 governs the outcome including the driver's compensation, and this clause yields to it.' The refund to the rider is not in dispute; the clause that fixes the driver's money on a wrong-face hold is POL-NS-03, and its compensation limb is limb (ii).

The two money movements are independent and are never netted: the rider's SGD 4.00 refund is a filing-party refund, while the SGD 2.00 goodwill is a platform-funded payment to the driver under POL-NS-03(ii). POL-GEN-03 requires both fields to be populated on a compound outcome and requires the ruling value to name the filing party's outcome, so the rider refund and the driver compensation should be recorded side by side.

To be straight about the size of the driver's remedy: POL-NS-07's 80 percent compensation is conditioned on POL-NS-01 being satisfied in full and on no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it. POL-NS-01 is not satisfied on this record, so the driver's entitlement is the SGD 2.00 POL-NS-03(ii) goodwill, not the SGD 3.20 POL-NS-07 would pay on a verified rider no-show.

The driver's profile is not a ground of decision in this case. POL-GEN-01 permits driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d to be read only for the POL-NS-07 anti-farming test, and POL-NS-07 is not engaged because POL-NS-01 is not satisfied; nothing in the driver's profile may be used to build an adverse finding against him on this trip.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the platform's own records decide this, and on the main point you both agree — the $4.00 cancellation fee cannot stand.

THE FEE. The driver never reached the pickup pin. His GPS trace carries 52 fixes across the whole window and not one of them falls inside the 120 m arrival radius for a LARGE_VENUE pickup; his closest approach to the pin over the entire trace was 284.95 m. POL-NS-01 limb (b) therefore fails. Limb (d) fails independently: the trip was terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which is not one of the three codes limb (d) accepts (RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE, EXCESSIVE_WAIT), and POL-NS-01 itself sends such a trip to POL-NS-03. With two limbs broken, the baseline chargeable no-show fails and the whole SGD 4.00 returns to the rider.

WHY POL-NS-03 GOVERNS, NOT POL-NS-06. [Driver] held position at the HarbourFront face of the venue: 284.95 m from the pin, outside the 120 m arrival radius but inside POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling, which the clause says is the whole test and is decidable from coordinates alone (no venue_id match is asserted — the pickup pin carries VEN-VIVOCITY and the driver's track carries none, so that corroboration is not established either way). The recorded wait of 6.6 minutes (395 seconds, against the 300-second LARGE_VENUE minimum) and the stationary 0.0 km/h reading show a hold, not an abandonment. POL-NS-02 says in terms that where the driver was stationary for the required dwell within 400 m of the pin, POL-NS-03 governs the outcome including the driver's compensation and POL-NS-02 yields to it. I therefore reject the rider-side POL-NS-06 argument that the zero in-geofence dwell strips the driver's payment: the refund is the same full $4.00 either way, but the driver's money is fixed by POL-NS-03, not by POL-NS-06.

FAULT AND THE DRIVER'S MONEY. The chat log holds exactly two messages and both are SYSTEM ('Driver assigned. Meet at VivoCity, Lobby L.' and 'Your driver has arrived'); neither party named an entrance, block, tower or bay, and trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 4 — two or more. POL-NS-03 limb (ii) therefore applies: this was pin ambiguity, not fault on either side. That limb gives [Driver] a platform-funded goodwill payment of 50 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee = SGD 2.00, charged to the platform and never recovered from [Rider]. [Driver], your POL-NS-07 claim of SGD 3.20 is rejected: that clause compensates only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not — so your remedy is the SGD 2.00 goodwill, not SGD 3.20. Under POL-GEN-03 the rider's SGD 4.00 refund and the driver's SGD 2.00 goodwill are independent and are never netted; the ruling value (FULL_REFUND) names the filing party's outcome.

CLAIMS NOT ACCEPTED. POL-NS-05 (false arrival) is not engaged: the only distance fact on the record is the 284.95 m closest approach, inside POL-NS-05's 300 m mark, and the clause's own carve-out sends a driver stationary within 300 m of the pin but outside the arrival radius to POL-NS-03. No false-arrival referral is therefore produced. POL-NS-04 (rider exoneration) is not engaged either: the chat log contains no rider message, so limb (a) cannot be run — but no adverse inference about rider location is drawn, since the rider's 31 fixes sit within 22.5 m of the pin, far inside the 150 m rider-presence radius. POL-NS-07 is not reached (above). POL-NS-09 escalation is not triggered: no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence; rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and both disputes_with_counterparty_90d fields are 0; the anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d 1 against completed_trips_30d 187); and no evidence is impaired under POL-NS-08.

EVIDENCE INTEGRITY AND WEIGHT. Nothing is impaired under POL-NS-08: the trace runs the full window at 100 percent coverage, 52 driver fixes, gaps empty and max gap 0 seconds, so limb (b) is not met; the chat log's 2 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count, so limb (c) is not met; the arrival marker falls inside the trace and the trip start and termination match the first and last fixes, so limb (a) is not met; and the fare line reconciles, so limb (d) is not met — the SGD 4.00 charged is the GREATER of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00). EV-ADVIS-00206-01 (TRAFFIC_ADVISORY) is MISSING with weight 0.0; its absence is citable and makes POL-NS-06 limb (i) unavailable, which supports the refund rather than changing it, and no deciding fact rests on it. The deciding facts rest on the GPS trace, trip record, chat log and fare breakdown, none of which is discounted, so confidence is not capped below 1.0. Finally, POL-GEN-01: the profiles of both parties are context only and are not used as a ground of decision against either of you.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
